question.text: For a Cat III AIF that accepts subscriptions and redemptions using daily NAV, the Valuation Day is BEST defined as:

answer.text: Any day the manager feels appropriate
Only the last day of the financial year
The day pre-determined by the AIF and communicated in offer documents, as the day by reference to which the NAV is determined

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the chapter: 'The Valuation Day is pre-determined by a Category III AIF, and communicated to the investors in its offer documents, as the day by reference to which the NAV of the Category III AIF is determined.' It can be month-end, daily (listed-only), or bespoke. **The Trap:** Manager discretion without disclosure is not permitted. Year-end-only fails monthly disclosure. Month-end-only is permitted but not exclusive. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B and XIX-C test Valuation Day. Cross-ref: MF regulations use similar 'cut-off' language. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Align subscription/redemption cut-off with fund admin's NAV-strike time (usually T+1 at 11am IST). Any subscription before cut-off uses same-day NAV; after cut-off uses next NAV - document to avoid 'stale NAV' arbitrage.
